verses.1:1: And the word of the Lord came to Jonah the son of Amittai, saying,
verses.1:2: "Arise and go to Nineveh, the great city, and preach in it, for the outcry of its wickedness has come up to Me."
verses.1:3: And Jonah arose to flee to Tarshish from the presence of the Lord, and he went down to Joppa; and he found a ship going to Tarshish, and paid his fare, and went aboard it to sail with them to Tarshish from the presence of the Lord.
verses.1:4: And the Lord raised up a wind upon the sea, and a great tempest arose in the sea, and the ship was in danger of being shattered.
verses.1:5: And the mariners were afraid, and cried out, each man to his god; and they cast the wares that were in the ship into the sea, to be lightened of them. But Jonah had gone down into the hold of the ship, and was sleeping and snoring.
verses.1:6: And the captain came to him and said to him, "Why are you snoring? Arise and call upon your god, so that God may rescue us and we may not perish."
verses.1:7: And each man said to his companion, "Come, let us cast lots and learn on whose account this calamity is among us." So they cast lots, and the lot fell upon Jonah.
verses.1:8: And they said to him, "Tell us, what is your occupation, and from where do you come, and from what country and from what people are you?"
verses.1:9: And he said to them, "I am a servant of the Lord, and I worship the Lord, the God of heaven, who made the sea and the dry land."
verses.1:10: Then the men feared with a great fear and said to him, "What is this that you have done?" For the men knew that he was fleeing from the presence of the Lord, because he had told them.
verses.1:11: And they said to him, "What shall we do to you, that the sea may subside from us?" For the sea kept advancing and raising up a greater tempest.
verses.1:12: And Jonah said to them, "Lift me up and cast me into the sea, and the sea will subside from you; for I know that because of me this great tempest is upon you."
verses.1:13: Yet the men strove hard to return to the land, and they could not, for the sea kept advancing and rising up even more against them.
verses.1:14: Therefore they cried out to the Lord and said, "By no means, O Lord! Let us not perish on account of this man's life, and do not lay righteous blood upon us; for You, O Lord, have done as You willed."
verses.1:15: Then they took Jonah and cast him out into the sea, and the sea stood still from its surging.
verses.1:16: And the men feared the Lord with a great fear, and offered sacrifices to the Lord and vowed vows.
verses.2:1: And the Lord commanded a great sea creature to swallow Jonah; and Jonah was in the belly of the sea creature three days and three nights.
verses.2:2: Then Jonah prayed to the Lord his God from the belly of the sea creature,
verses.2:3: and said, "I cried out in my affliction to the Lord my God, and He heard me. Out of the belly of Hades You heard the voice of my cry; You cast me into the depths of the heart of the sea,
verses.2:4: and rivers surrounded me; all Your towering billows and Your waves passed over me.
verses.2:5: And I said, 'I have been cast out from Your eyes; shall I indeed look again toward Your holy temple?'
verses.2:6: Water was poured around me even to the soul; the lowest deep encircled me; my head sank down into the clefts of the mountains.
verses.2:7: I went down into a land whose bars are everlasting restraints; yet let the corruption of my life ascend, O Lord my God.
verses.2:8: When my soul was failing from me, I remembered the Lord; and may my prayer come to You, into Your holy temple.
verses.2:9: Those who observe vain and false things have forsaken their mercy.
verses.2:10: But I will sacrifice to You with a voice of praise and thanksgiving; all that I have vowed I will pay to You for deliverance, to the Lord."
verses.2:11: And command was given to the sea creature, and it cast Jonah out upon the dry land.
verses.3:1: And the word of the Lord came to Jonah a second time, saying,
verses.3:2: "Arise, go to Nineveh, the great city, and preach in it according to the former proclamation which I spoke to you."
verses.3:3: So Jonah arose and went to Nineveh, just as the Lord had spoken. Now Nineveh was a great city to God, about a journey of three days.
verses.3:4: And Jonah began to enter into the city about one day's journey, and he preached and said, "Yet three days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown!"
verses.3:5: And the men of Nineveh believed in God, and proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloth, from the greatest of them to the least of them.
verses.3:6: And the word reached the king of Nineveh; and he rose up from his throne, and removed his robe from himself, and wrapped himself in sackcloth, and sat upon ashes.
verses.3:7: And it was proclaimed and spoken in Nineveh from the king and from his nobles, saying, "Let men and beasts, and oxen and sheep, taste nothing; neither let them graze, nor let them drink water."
verses.3:8: And the men and the beasts wrapped themselves in sackcloth, and cried out earnestly to God; and each one turned back from his evil way and from the unrighteousness that was in their hands, saying,
verses.3:9: "Who knows whether God will relent and turn back from the fury of His wrath, so that we shall by no means perish?"
verses.3:10: And God saw their works, that they had turned back from their evil ways; and God relented concerning the calamity which He had spoken to do to them, and He did not do it.
verses.4:1: And Jonah was grieved with a great grief, and he was confounded.
verses.4:2: And he prayed to the Lord and said, "O Lord, were not these my words while I was still in my land? Therefore I hastened beforehand to flee to Tarshish, for I knew that You are merciful and compassionate, longsuffering and abundant in mercy, and relenting over calamities.
verses.4:3: And now, O Sovereign Lord, take my life from me, for to die is better for me than to live."
verses.4:4: And the Lord said to Jonah, "Are you exceedingly grieved?"
verses.4:5: And Jonah went out from the city and sat opposite the city; and he made a booth for himself there and sat beneath it in the shade, until he should see what would become of the city.
verses.4:6: And the Lord God commanded a gourd, and it grew up over the head of Jonah to be a shade above his head, to shade him from his afflictions; and Jonah rejoiced over the gourd with a great joy.
verses.4:7: And God commanded a worm at dawn on the next day, and it struck the gourd, and it withered away.
verses.4:8: And it came to pass, as soon as the sun rose, that God commanded a scorching wind of burning heat, and the sun struck upon the head of Jonah; and he grew faint and despaired of his life, and said, "To die is better for me than to live."
verses.4:9: And God said to Jonah, "Are you exceedingly grieved over the gourd?" And he said, "I am exceedingly grieved, even to death."
verses.4:10: And the Lord said, "You had pity on the gourd, over which you did not endure hardship, nor did you nurture it, which came into being in a night and in a night perished.
verses.4:11: And shall I not have pity on Nineveh, the great city, in which dwell more than one hundred twenty thousand people who do not know their right hand or their left hand, and much livestock?"

notes.1:2: Greek reads "preach in it" and "the outcry of its wickedness," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "cry out against it" and omits "the outcry of."
notes.1:9: Greek reads "a servant of the Lord" (doulos Kyriou), contrasting with "a Hebrew" in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.1:14: Greek reads "righteous blood" (haima dikaion), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "innocent blood."
notes.2:1: Verse numbering in chapter 2 follows the Septuagint (where 2:1 corresponds to 1:17 in most English Bibles); Greek ketos denotes a great sea creature or sea monster rather than specifically a fish.
notes.2:6: Greek reads "my head sank down into the clefts of the mountains," differing from the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("seaweed was wrapped around my head").
notes.2:7: Greek reads literally "let the corruption of my life ascend" (a third-person imperative), whereas the Hebrew reads "You brought up my life from the pit."
notes.2:11: Greek uses a passive verb ("command was given to the sea creature") rather than the Hebrew active ("the LORD spoke to the fish").
notes.3:2: Greek specifies "according to the former proclamation which I spoke to you," referring back to the initial commission in 1:2, whereas the Hebrew reads "the proclamation that I tell you."
notes.3:4: The Septuagint reads "three days," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "forty days."
notes.3:8: In the Greek text, the verbs in verse 8 are past-tense indicatives narrating the Ninevites' actual response rather than imperatives continuing the king's decree as in the Hebrew; accordingly, "saying" introduces the people's words in verse 9.
notes.4:1: The Septuagint renders Jonah's reaction as intense grief and confusion ("grieved with a great grief, and he was confounded"), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text describes him as displeased and angry.
notes.4:4: The Septuagint asks "Are you exceedingly grieved?" (echoed in 4:9), where the Hebrew Masoretic Text asks whether Jonah does well to be angry.
notes.4:6: The Greek kolokynthe specifically denotes a gourd plant, famous in patristic translation debates; the Septuagint also reads "to shade him from his afflictions" rather than "to deliver him."
notes.4:8: The Greek verb apelegeto ("despaired of" or "renounced") conveys giving up on one's life, paralleling the Hebrew idiom for asking to die.
